nodes.label: White-on-White Preview Bug Class
nodes.summary: Near-white preview canvases (bg-background, bg-primary/[0.03]) cause light text colours to vanish — merchant sees nothing, assumes the setting didn't apply, and may commit bad styling. Same trap repeats on every preview surface that isn't explicitly contrast-hardened.

nodes.label: Neutral Mid-Tone Canvas Rule
nodes.summary: Every admin preview surface must use bg-foreground/[0.05] with ring-1 ring-foreground/5 — never bg-background or bg-card — so that both light and dark text colour picks remain visible regardless of the active theme.

nodes.label: Foreground-Tint Preview Canvas Formula
nodes.summary: bg-foreground/[0.05] resolves to ~5% opacity of the theme's dark foreground token, yielding a soft mid-gray on both light and dark themes. Paired with ring-1 ring-foreground/5 it visually signals 'this is a preview frame' while guaranteeing contrast for any merchant colour choice.

nodes.label: Self-Contrast-Aware Preset Rule
nodes.summary: A preset that uses a light text colour (e.g. brand-muted) must still read on the neutral preview canvas — 'muted text on muted-bg' is a preset authoring error, not a canvas error. Presets carry the elegant feel through weight and tracking, not through low-contrast colour.

nodes.label: Light + Dark Theme Detection Recipe for Preview Audit
nodes.summary: Verification matrix: open each preview surface with (light theme + muted-text preset), (dark theme + foreground-text preset), and (brand-primary chip bg + white text). If any combination is invisible the canvas choice is wrong — fix the canvas, not the individual preset.

nodes.label: Preview Canvas Anti-Patterns
nodes.summary: Three anti-patterns to refuse: (1) bg-card / bg-background — clean but kills light text; (2) patching individual presets to use darker text — symptom fix that breaks new presets; (3) hardcoded #f5f5f5 — breaks dark-mode merchants with the inverse problem.

nodes.label: Global Reset Escape-Hatch Pattern
nodes.summary: Any admin config form exposing >10 fields ships a destructive 'Reset all' button alongside Save. Confirms via locale-aware confirm(), writes a truly-blank state via the same PUT endpoint, and toasts the result. Turns experimentation from risky to safe — no support ticket needed to recover.

nodes.label: Destructive Button Styling Requirement
nodes.summary: Reset buttons must use border-destructive/40 + text-destructive (red border/text) so they are visually distinct from the primary Save action. Placement must be near Save — not a separate danger zone at the bottom — so the merchant sees the visual warning in the same eye scan.

nodes.label: Blank State, Not Baked Defaults Rule
nodes.summary: Reset must write a truly-empty state (e.g. { fonts: [], zones: {} }) — NOT a 'factory defaults' object. Baked-in defaults become stale when templates change and leave merchants stuck with someone else's old opinions. The storefront's inheritance from the active template is the real default.

nodes.label: Locale-Aware Confirm Dialog Rule
nodes.summary: Destructive confirm() dialogs must render in the active UI locale — Arabic merchants must not see an English warning they may not parse. The bilingual confirm string must be derived from the same isAr flag used throughout the admin UI.

nodes.label: Safe-Experimentation Loop Principle
nodes.summary: Live preview (iterate without committing) + quick presets (known-good starting points) + global reset (one-click recovery) together form a closed loop: merchants can experiment freely knowing they can always get back to a clean slate. Any admin config UI missing one leg of this loop creates friction or risk.

nodes.label: Reset Uses Same Save Endpoint Rule
nodes.summary: The Reset action must call the same PUT endpoint as Save with a blank payload — not a dedicated delete endpoint. This ensures reset goes through the same Zod validation, audit log, and idempotency guarantees as normal saves, preventing column corruption or audit gaps.
